Pulse AI – Intelligent Timesheet & Invoicing Assistant
Important: UI-specific details in this version are proposed from the current product plan and must be reconciled with the approved mockup when available.
Initial PRD/FSD based on current Emerson requirements, architecture and Pulse AI product plan. Mockup-specific details remain proposed/TBD.
Emerson Employee Timesheet and Workforce Management System requirements/SRS.
Pulse AI architecture/reference document covering AI validation, approval, payroll/invoice preparation and role-based dashboards.
Current Pulse AI product/design implementation plan, including proposed employee, manager, HR, finance and director workflows.

Pulse AI is a centralized, role-based workforce application for recording employee work hours, validating timesheet data, managing approvals, preparing payroll-ready and invoice-ready outputs, monitoring compliance, and enabling permission-aware AI assistance. The product is intended to reduce manual verification effort, improve visibility of missing or unusual entries, and provide traceable workflows from time entry through downstream finance preparation.

Manual or fragmented timesheet processes can produce incorrect entries, missing submissions, slow managerial review, and additional effort for HR and Finance. Pulse AI addresses these issues through structured time entry, deterministic validation, AI-assisted anomaly detection, approval workflows, notifications, role-based dashboards, and controlled downstream preparation.
Provide a simple centralized experience for employees to record and submit work hours.
Reduce invalid, incomplete, duplicate, or unusual timesheet entries before downstream processing.
Give managers a traceable approval/rejection workflow with clear evidence and revision history.
Enable HR to maintain workforce data and monitor submission compliance.
Enable Finance to prepare controlled payroll-ready summaries and invoice drafts from approved time.
Provide directors with organization-level operational visibility while respecting sensitive-data permissions.
Provide notifications and reminders for actionable workflow events.
Provide a read-oriented, permission-aware AI assistant for authorized workforce and timesheet questions.
Pulse AI must not be represented as a full payroll tax engine unless Emerson explicitly confirms those rules.
AI anomalies do not automatically approve or reject timesheets; accountable users retain decision authority.
The AI assistant must not execute arbitrary database queries or bypass role permissions.
ERP, biometric, attendance, Teams/email, and other enterprise integrations remain optional/TBD until interfaces are confirmed.
Exact salary calculation, overtime, leave, bonus, deduction, billing-rate and invoice rules remain TBD.
Enter, save, review and submit own timesheet; see status/history; receive reminders; use permitted AI assistance.
Own records and explicitly authorized data.
Review assigned employees; approve/reject; inspect validation/anomaly evidence; monitor missing submissions.
Maintain employee master data; import/validate workforce data; monitor compliance; audit HR actions.
HR scope; compensation only if separately authorized.
View approved hours; prepare payroll-ready exports and invoice drafts; trace outputs to source time.
View organization-level submission, approval, allocation and exception analytics.
Broad reporting scope; sensitive detail remains permission controlled.
HR establishes or imports employee records and role/scope assignments.
Employee enters work hours in the active timesheet period; the system validates required fields and obvious invalid values.
AI/detection services may flag unusual patterns, duplicates, missing hours or other configured anomalies.
Employee reviews and submits the period.
The submitted timesheet is routed to the appropriate manager approval workflow.
Manager reviews evidence and approves or rejects with a reason; rejected submissions return to the employee for correction/resubmission.
Approved time becomes eligible for authorized Finance preparation workflows.
Finance previews payroll-ready exports and/or invoice drafts, with traceability back to approved source entries.
Dashboards, notifications, audit history and the AI assistant provide role-appropriate visibility throughout.
Users shall authenticate before accessing protected product functions.
Role- and scope-based authorization shall restrict employee, timesheet, salary/compensation and organization data.
Employees shall enter and submit working hours associated with their employee identity and period.
The product should support a draft-to-review-to-submit journey with visible save/autosave state.
The product shall prevent/flag invalid numeric values, negative hours and missing required fields; exact hour limits are configurable/TBD.
The product shall support detection/flagging of missing hours, duplicate entries and unusual patterns.
Submitted entries shall be routed for managerial sign-off; exact approval levels are TBD.
A rejection should require a reason and support employee correction/resubmission with revision visibility.
The product shall identify missing submissions and generate actionable alerts/reminders; channels and schedule are TBD.
HR shall be able to upload/manage employee information; exact fields and file format are TBD.
Approved work-hour data shall support payroll-ready summaries and invoice preparation.
Finance outputs should visibly trace to approved source timesheets and exclude ineligible/unapproved time.
Role-based dashboards shall provide submission, approval and relevant workforce insights.
A generative AI assistant shall support authorized queries and summaries without exposing unauthorized information.
Material workflow actions should be auditable, including submissions, approvals/rejections, imports and finance preparation.
Because the approved mockup is not currently available, this map is the Version 1 product baseline. It should be reconciled screen-by-screen once the mockup is received.
Authentication entry, error state, role-aware post-login routing.
Sidebar/header, current role/scope, notifications, user menu, AI assistant entry.
Current period status, missing-hours alerts, recent submissions and shortcuts.
Time-entry grid/day editor, totals, validation, anomaly explanations, save state and submit action.
Period summary, blocking issues/warnings, confirmation and resulting status.
Previous periods, statuses, detail and rejected-period correction/resubmission.
Pending submissions, filters, missing submissions, anomalies and assigned-team scope.
Entry detail, validation/anomaly evidence, approve/reject, revision comparison.
Upload → map → validate → commit, row-level errors and result summary.
Approved-hour filters, exceptions and downstream eligibility.
Preview, controlled generation, history/detail; no implied tax calculation.
Billable/uninvoiced view, draft detail and source-timesheet traceability.
Submission/approval health, allocation trends, material exceptions and period comparison.
Read/unread state, actionable deep links, reminder/approval/finance/security categories.
Visible role/scope context, suggested queries, sourced results, privacy/read-only notices.
Timesheet entry should require minimal steps and make blocking errors distinct from warnings and AI anomalies.
Status, period and permission scope should remain visible on workflow-critical screens.
Keyboard interaction and clear focus states should be supported for primary data-entry and review workflows.
Tables and charts should provide readable labels and accessible alternatives/summaries.
Empty, loading, error, permission-denied and success states should be explicitly designed.
Sensitive or restricted fields should be clearly marked and omitted when the user lacks permission.
Authenticated APIs, enforced authorization, least-privilege access, protected salary/compensation data.
Submitted data must be stored reliably; prevent accidental loss and provide appropriate error handling.
Normal user operations should respond within acceptable enterprise-web expectations; frequently used queries should be optimized.
Architecture should support growth in employees, departments, managers and organizational units without major redesign.
Clear workflows, minimal steps for timesheet entry, actionable notifications and understandable AI output.
Material state changes and controlled outputs should be traceable to actor, time, scope and source record.
Lower rate of incomplete/invalid submissions reaching managers or Finance.
Traceable payroll/invoice preparation with fewer source-data discrepancies.
AI assistant responses remain within user authorization scope.
Daily, weekly or monthly submission policy; current product plan assumes a weekly experience but stakeholder confirmation is required.
Whether submitted/approved timesheets can be edited and under what state transition.
Number of approval levels, assignment rules, delegation/escalation and bulk-approval policy.
Expected daily/weekly hours, overtime, leave, project/task allocation and acceptable limits.
Employee fields, file format, create/update semantics and error-handling policy.
Salary calculation vs. storage, payroll export schema, deductions/bonus/leave rules, billing rates, invoice rules.
Channel(s), reminder timing, recipients, escalation and retry behavior.
Exact anomaly thresholds/model, supported assistant tools/queries, model/API, retention and external-LLM data policy.
Identity provider, ERP/HRMS, attendance, email/Teams, payroll/invoice systems and available APIs.
Final screen list, navigation, field labels, component placement and interaction details.

This PRD is suitable as a baseline for design and engineering discussion. It is not a final UI contract. When the approved mockup and remaining Emerson business rules are available, the document should be revised to map every visible screen, field, action and state to a confirmed requirement.
